core_message: Underground organs are central to perenniality, storage, vegetative propagation, and post-disturbance regrowth, but the field lacks a cross-species omics framework.
Existing studies are often species-specific or organ-specific, making it difficult to compare rhizomes, tubers, storage roots, corm-like stems, and related underground structures.
UGO-Omics integrates a 51-species underground-organ atlas with an 11-species high-confidence analytical backbone.
An independent BUSCO-based phylogenetic framework places the 11-species backbone into an evolutionary context.
Sequence-to-UGO, Gene-list-to-UGO, Resource Finder, Organ Kits, demo results, and use cases make the platform directly usable by researchers.
UGO-Omics identifies a recurrent regeneration–resilience core toolkit spanning meristem/regrowth, stress resilience, hormone-related regulation, and developmental regulatory modules.
Known-category recovery shows that the current module layer recovers expected biological categories relevant to underground-organ development and persistence.
The integrated discovery case supports a module-level convergence model in which diverse underground organs repeatedly recruit a conserved regeneration–resilience toolkit.
